General H-prime=1/g yields derivative H(y(x))=y-prime/g(y)=f(x). This uses chain rule on nonzero-g range. Roots of g yield constant solutions, but without uniqueness assumptions this does not classify every possible piecewise solution that reaches a root.
Choose a connected y-interval with continuous nonzero g; H-prime has fixed sign and H is invertible there. Domain must keep F(x)+C inside H range. H=ln|y| needs a sign branch.

For y-prime=2y/x on x nonzero, derivative of y/x² is (xy-prime-2y)/x³=0. Hence y=ax² separately on each connected half-line. ODE does not hold at x=0. Different constants either side can still give a C1 extension at0; C2 extension forces the same constant. Do not claim mere smoothness loosely establishes one global ODE solution.
